primitives.name: Incremental Dataflow
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model - Two-layer design: Python layer builds/optimizes the computation graph (transpiles to high-level dataflow, then to an internal dataflow assembly in Rust); the Rust runtime (modified subset of differential dataflow + custom operators on a modified LSM tree) executes both batch and streaming.
primitives.assumptions: Computation graph is acyclic and supports incremental updates; Rust runtime maintains deterministic execution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When graph contains cycles or unbounded recursion.

layer2.mapping: The Python Table API translates to a Rust-based dataflow kernel, preserving semantic equivalence between batch and streaming modes.
layer2.telemetry: Throughput and latency metrics across batch and streaming modes.

primitives.name: Delta Propagation
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Table API: collections of typed columns sharing an identifier set; inserts/deletes/modifications propagate as deltas.
primitives.assumptions: All modifications are idempotent and propagate consistently across the system.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When identifier collisions occur or propagation order is ambiguous.

layer2.mapping: Deltas enable efficient recomputation of downstream states in response to input changes, supporting iterative algorithms like PageRank.
layer2.telemetry: Replay consistency and backfilling success rate.

primitives.name: Deterministic Replay
primitives.verbatim_quote: Bounded streams replay to identical results (deterministic modulo user-defined nondeterministic callbacks).
primitives.assumptions: Input stream is bounded and commit messages control output progression.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When external callbacks introduce randomness or non-determinism.

layer2.mapping: Replay behavior mirrors batch execution exactly, enabling validation of real-time pipelines against historical data.
layer2.telemetry: Bit-identical output comparison between batch and streaming runs.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in a dual-layer architecture where Python constructs a high-level dataflow graph, which is then compiled into a Rust-based execution engine. This allows for seamless transition between batch and streaming paradigms without code duplication. The system achieves parity by ensuring that each operation in the dataflow graph is incrementally updated, and changes propagate as deltas. The deterministic replay mechanism ensures that the same inputs produce identical outputs regardless of whether they are processed in batch or streaming mode. This is achieved through explicit control over commit points and absence of watermarking. The system supports iterative algorithms such as PageRank by maintaining consistent state updates even when new data arrives in batches. The key mathematical duality is between the symbolic representation of operations in Python and their concrete realization in Rust, with the delta propagation serving as the bridge between these layers.
